oewn-07259785-n.learner: the act of getting someone to believe or do something, or of trying to; words meant to make someone believe something or act on it
examples: nor did Sir William at all shake her purpose by his attempt at persuasion
To yield readily--easily--to the persuasion of a friend is no merit with you.

oewn-05954491-n.learner: something a person believes or judges to be true without proof that it is
examples: nothing but a persuasion of my being indifferent would have prevented his coming down again

oewn-00556685-n.learner: the act of moving fast and without care
examples: Well, Jane, make haste and tell us; make haste, my love.
In his haste he knocked the cup off the table.

connotation.why: the fast moving is treated as careless

oewn-05067358-n.learner: speed that is more eager than it should be, and that may bring carelessness with it
examples: He regretted his haste in accepting the first offer he was given.

connotation.why: the speed is judged to be more than it should have been

oewn-14474655-n.learner: a state in which something is urgent, so that you have to move fast
examples: There is no haste; the coach does not leave until noon.

oewn-04647895-n.learner: a calm, kind willingness to put up with waiting or with people who do things badly
examples: I recollected my dear Elizabeth and Jane, and for their sakes had patience with her.
She tried, however, to compose herself to answer him with patience

connotation.why: the putting up with it is praised as good-natured

oewn-00496535-n.learner: a card game that one person plays alone
examples: She dealt out the cards for a game of patience.

oewn-07591549-n.learner: a small evening meal, eaten early in the evening if the main meal was at midday, or late at night before bed
examples: they would have a nice comfortable noisy game of lottery tickets, and a little bit of hot supper afterwards
They solaced their wretchedness, however, by duets after supper

oewn-08273488-n.learner: a party at which a small evening meal is served
examples: The Lucases gave a supper for their neighbours, and everyone stayed late.

oewn-14474655-n.learner: a state in which something is urgent, so that you have to move fast
examples: he was in such a hurry to be gone, and his spirits so greatly discomposed
All that I can promise you, therefore, is not to be in a hurry.

oewn-00556685-n.learner: the act of moving fast and without care
examples: could serve only to amuse her in the hurry and confusion of the following hour

connotation.why: the fast moving is treated as careless

oewn-05067358-n.learner: speed that is more eager than it should be, and that may bring carelessness with it
examples: He was sorry afterwards for the hurry with which he had written the letter.

connotation.why: the speed is judged to be more than it should have been

oewn-00103071-v.learner: to turn red in the face, as a person does when embarrassed or ashamed
examples: Elizabeth blushed and blushed again with shame and vexation.
She blushed at the very idea

oewn-00289921-v.learner: to turn pink or a little red
examples: The apples blushed as they ripened on the tree.

oewn-00178467-r.learner: many times, one time after another

oewn-13793430-n.learner: a small number of something, with no exact count given

oewn-13765745-n.learner: two things of the same kind

oewn-01776881-v.learner: to stir up a feeling, or to draw one out

oewn-02120601-v.learner: to stir up feelings in a person or a group of people
examples: The promise of a ball excited the younger girls.

oewn-01765558-v.learner: to stir up someone's feelings or emotions, or to disturb their calm
examples: The sudden news excited her so much that she could not sit still.
